meta.headline: Every Leap Second So Far Was Added; None Was Ever Taken Away
meta.seoTitle: Have Any Leap Seconds Ever Been Removed?

dek.text: Since UTC began in 1972, every leap second on record has lengthened the civil clock, and none has ever shortened it.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has been added to civil time; none has ever been taken away.

description.text: The official table behind UTC lists every leap second since 1972; each one made the civil clock a second longer, and none has ever made it shorter.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has been added to civil time; none has ever been taken away.

sentences.text: The International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service's own table of TAI minus UTC opens at 10 seconds on 1 January 1972 and closes at 37 seconds on 1 January 2017, with every entry in between exactly one second higher than the last.

assertions.text: The IERS table of TAI-UTC lists values from 10 s on 1 January 1972 to 37 s on 1 January 2017, each exactly one second larger than the one before.

sentences.text: In other words, the civil clock has only ever gained a second from this table; it has never lost one.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has been added to civil time; none has ever been taken away.
